comment: TOML DECLARATION ORDER AND THE EMPTY KEY, authored from the TOML v1.0.0 specification before observing the corrected output. Two rulings, both found by the 1,140-file census rather than by a fixture, and both pinned here for the first time. (1) DECLARATION ORDER IS NOT SIGNIFICANT: the spec requires no super-table to be written first, so `[late.child.grandchild]` written above `[late.child]` is valid TOML and `late.child.grandchild` is INSIDE `late.child`. A walk that resolves an owner from a document-order map files it under the FILE, and the `contains` edge then points at the module instead of at the table that contains the section. Measured: 1 occurrence in 1,140 files, `ansible/pyproject.toml`, where `[tool.setuptools.dynamic]` is on line 45 and `[tool.setuptools]` on line 49. (2) AN EMPTY KEY PRODUCES NOTHING, AT EVERY LEVEL: `"" = 1` names nothing because an identity needs a name. That decision was pinned at the DOCUMENT ROOT, where a guard existed; inside a table there was no guard and the path is built as `${table}.${key}`, so an empty segment became a TRAILING DOT — `pb-grpc/pyproject.toml:53` published `tool.setuptools.package-dir.`, which TOML cannot parse back. The `forbidRelationships` rows are the load-bearing half: a symbol whose name ends in a bare `.` still resolves inside its own file, so no resolution-rate check can see it, and only an explicit prohibition catches it.

expectSymbols.comment: declared on line 22, before BOTH of its ancestors. Its NAME was always right; what the census found wrong was its CONTAINMENT, which is why this row pairs with the relationship row below and no symbol assertion could have seen the defect.

expectSymbols.comment: the key BESIDE the empty one still publishes — the ruling omits the unnamed key, not the section that contains it

forbidSymbols.name: table.with.empty.key.
forbidSymbols.comment: THE defect, on the corpus file that produced it: `[tool.setuptools.package-dir]` followed by `"" = "src/python/grpcio"` published `tool.setuptools.package-dir.` at line 53 of `pb-grpc/pyproject.toml`. It is not a spelling TOML can parse back, so the identity does not round-trip.

forbidSymbols.name: table.with.empty.key.""
forbidSymbols.comment: the empty key, spelled the round-trippable way, is still omitted — the lane's recorded decision is that an empty name is not an identity. Pinned AT THIS LEVEL here; `toml/malformed-and-rejected` pins it at the document root, where the guard happened to be.
the document-level spelling, omitted by `toml/malformed-and-rejected`. Re-stated so a reader of THIS fixture does not have to open another one to learn the rule.

forbidSymbols.name: late.child.grandchild.
forbidSymbols.comment: no name may end in a bare `.`, at any level. The shape resolves inside its own file, so no resolution-rate check and no confidence check can see it — only an explicit prohibition can.

expectRelationships.comment: this edge is UNCHANGED by the fix — `[late.child]` at line 28 already had its ancestor at line 25 above it. Pinned so a reader can see the second pass did not move everything.

THE CORRECTION. `[late.child.grandchild]` is on line 22 and BOTH its ancestors are declared below it, so a document-order walk emits this edge from the MODULE. A symbol assertion cannot see the difference — only the edge's SOURCE can, which is why the matching `forbidRelationships` row exists.
a key hangs off its own SECTION's allocated name, so re-owning the section does not move it
the CORRECT source for this edge — `[only]` is declared on line 35, three lines AFTER the section it contains
declared AFTER the section it contains; nothing about its OWN edge changes
the section still publishes its OTHER key: the ruling omits the unnamed key, not the section

forbidRelationships.comment: THE MISOWNED EDGE. This is what a document-order walk emits and what the second pass replaces. An expectation file cannot ask for the absence of a correct row and the presence of the correct one at once, so the correct row is in `expectRelationships` and this one is here.
same, for the single-ancestor shape `ansible/pyproject.toml` actually has. The CORRECT row for this edge is in `expectRelationships` with `from: only`.

THE EDGE WITH THE MALFORMED TARGET. Production drops it in `filterNoiseRelationships` because the leaf after the trailing `.` is empty, so it never reaches the graph — but the SYMBOL is published, and a symbol is what search, the docs engine and the store index. Pinned as forbidden so the fixture states the intent even where the pipeline hides it.
